subject: Cognitive Science
title: Babbling and First Words
description: A short lesson to help you apply Babbling and First Words.

hook.text: At six months a baby babbles "ba-ba-ba." By twelve months "ba-ba" becomes "ball." Meaning arrives.

buildup.text: Babbling follows a universal sequence: cooing at two months, canonical babbling by six months.

discovery.text: Even deaf babies babble—with their hands. Sign-exposed children produce manual babbling on time.

twist.text: First words are mostly nouns for objects kids can act on. "Ball" appears across nearly every language.

climax.text: Around eighteen months, the vocabulary explosion hits. Children learn up to ten words per day.

punchline.text: From babble to words in twelve months flat.

quiz.question: What do deaf babies do instead of vocal babbling?
